subject: 南京大报恩寺旧琉璃塔（据1915年土山湾模型绘制）
source_note: 原塔已毁。采用1915年土山湾孤儿院工坊制作的旧塔模型实拍，非现代玻璃新塔；模型照片为2024年ScribblingGeek拍摄。以九层塔身、底部副檐、八角轮廓和金属塔刹链饰为依据作线稿意象，非测绘复原。
author: ScribblingGeek
prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the delicate thin black-ink STYLE MASTER. Image 2 is the actual 1915 Tushanwan MODEL PHOTO of the historical Porcelain Tower of Nanjing, the subject and architectural geometry. Image 3 is the CURRENT ILLUSTRATION TO EDIT. Work directly on image 3. Add one whole occupied storey immediately ABOVE the broad ground-floor skirt roof and BELOW the lowest existing arched-window balcony. This new storey must have a full-height wall band with arched windows, a balcony railing, and a projecting pagoda roof, just like the storey directly above it. Physically lengthen the tower by one floor; make all existing upper floors slightly shorter if necessary to fit the portrait frame. The current image has 7 rows of upper arched windows. The finished image must have 8 rows of upper arched windows plus the ground-floor entrance, nine floors in all. Do not treat the tiny closed strip under the bottom balcony as a floor. Do not return an unchanged 7-row tower. All other features remain: ring finial and chains, octagonal tower facets, base hall, staircase, symmetrical alignment, delicate black lines on pure white, no colors, no fills, no labels. Entire tower complete within portrait 1024x1536 canvas. The only substantive edit is insertion of this full extra window-and-balcony storey.
initial_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE line drawing. Use confident fine contours with a few finer internal structural lines. All surfaces remain WHITE; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, no broad grey shading, no crosshatching, no pencil grain, no texture, no gradient. No color, no gold, no black background. The white will become transparent and the ink uniformly gold in the website.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Portrait 1024×1536, entire pagoda occupies about 84% of canvas height, centered with generous equal side margins, apex and base uncut.
Subject: historical 南京大报恩寺琉璃塔, the ORIGINAL Porcelain Tower of Nanjing, destroyed in the nineteenth century, using the documented 1915 Tushanwan workshop model photographed in image 2 as the geometry reference. This is a model-based historical evocation, NOT the modern glass tower. Preserve the octagonal tapering tower with its nine storeys, the projecting eaves and railings, the especially wide ground-level skirt roof, central entry stair, and tall metal ring finial with curved hanging chains. Maintain all roof tiers visible in the model (the ground storey has an additional skirt eave), do not turn it into a generic Chinese pagoda. Rotate slightly toward a centered front elevation with central entry centered and visible octagonal side facets. Remove museum displays, pedestal, room, and all surrounding models. Omit dense miniature polychrome ornament; simple arched openings and balcony outlines only, all white inside. No hatching, black wall panels, black windows or text. Keep finial chains as thin continuous curving lines with only a few bead indications.
Mandatory precise construction sequence, count carefully BEFORE drawing: this historical tower must have EIGHT upper occupied window-and-balcony levels above its ground entry hall. From TOP DOWN draw: upper level A, then upper level B, then upper level C, then upper level D, then upper level E, then upper level F, then upper level G, then upper level H, then the broad ground entry hall I. Nine occupied levels total. Each of A-H requires its own distinct row of arched windows, its own continuous balcony railing, and its own eave. The ground entry hall I is wider and has the entrance and broad skirt eave. Never omit level H immediately above the wide ground hall. Portrait page: finial occupies y 4%-14%; upper A y 17%-23%, B 25%-31%, C 33%-39%, D 41%-47%, E 49%-55%, F 57%-63%, G 65%-71%, H 73%-79%; ground hall I y 82%-92%; steps y 92%-96%. These are invisible layout guides only; DO NOT draw letters, numbering or labels. Eight identical but gradually widening stacked upper sections can be rendered slightly shorter to fit. Prioritize accurate floor count over all small decorative detail.
